string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing has been the capital of China for most of the past seven hundred years and remains the political, cultural and diplomatic centre of the country. Imperial rule left behind the Forbidden City, the Temple of Heaven and the Ming city walls, while the modern city is arranged around a series of ring roads with Tiananmen Square at its heart. Beijing hosted the Summer Olympic Games in 2008 and in 2022 became the first city to stage both a Summer and a Winter Games. It also holds many of the leading universities, research institutes and technology firms.

Shanghai is the largest city in China by urban population and its leading financial and commercial centre. It grew from a treaty port opened to foreign trade in the nineteenth century into an industrial and shipping power, and the Bund still preserves the banks and trading houses of that period. Across the Huangpu River, Pudong and Lujiazui form a modern skyline of towers and stock exchanges. The port of Shanghai handles more container traffic than any other port in the world. The city is also known for its art deco buildings, its theatres and the lane houses of former foreign concessions.

Tianjin is one of the four direct-administered municipalities of China, governed by the central government rather than by a province. It lies on the coast of the Bohai Sea about 120 kilometres southeast of Beijing, where the Hai River meets the Grand Canal. The city developed as a major port and industrial base, and the Binhai New Area now hosts aerospace, electronics and petrochemical plants. Foreign concessions in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries left a distinctive mix of European-style buildings along the river. Tianjin also has a free trade zone, several large universities and a high-speed rail link to the capital.

Chongqing is a direct-administered municipality in southwest China and the only one located in the interior of the country. It was separated from Sichuan province and made a municipality in 1997, partly to manage resettlement for the Three Gorges Dam. Covering roughly 82,000 square kilometres, it is the largest municipality by area, with a permanent population of about 32 million. The city centre stands on a hilly peninsula where the Yangtze and Jialing rivers meet, giving it a dramatic skyline and famously steep streets. It is a major manufacturing base for cars, electronics and machinery, and its hotpot is known nationwide.
